authoredSolutions.50: Entropy falls when a system becomes more ordered or loses gas molecules. (A) Water freezing to ice at \(0^{\circ}C\): a liquid becomes an ordered solid, so \(\Delta S < 0\). (B) Freezing at \(-10^{\circ}C\) (supercooled water): still liquid to solid, so \(\Delta S_{sys} < 0\); the change is spontaneous only because the surroundings gain more entropy from the heat released. (C) \(\mathrm{N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightarrow 2NH_3(g)}\): 4 mol of gas become 2 mol, so \(\Delta S < 0\). (D) Adsorption of CO on a lead surface: gas molecules are held on the surface and lose freedom of motion, so \(\Delta S < 0\). (E) Dissolving NaCl in water: the ordered lattice breaks into mobile hydrated ions, so \(\Delta S > 0\). Entropy decreases in (A), (B), (C) and (D), option (A).

\[(t-2)^{2}=10\left(t+\tfrac{18}{5}\right)=10t+36.\]
Thus \(t^{2}-14t-32=0\Rightarrow (t-16)(t+2)=0\Rightarrow t=16\), so \(4^{x}=16\Rightarrow x=2\).
Substituting \(x=2\), the matrix becomes
\[\begin{vmatrix} 3 & 1 & 4 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \end{vmatrix}.\]
Expanding along the first row: \(3(0-2)-1(0-4)+4(1-0)=-6+4+4=2.\)

Let the first \(2n\) numbers have variance \(\sigma_1^{2}\) (mean \(6\)) and the last \(n\) have variance \(\sigma_2^{2}\) (mean \(3\)). Overall mean \(=\dfrac{2n\cdot6+n\cdot3}{3n}=5\). Combined variance \(=4\):
\[\frac{2n(\sigma_1^{2}+(6-5)^{2})+n(\sigma_2^{2}+(3-5)^{2})}{3n}=4\Rightarrow 2\sigma_1^{2}+\sigma_2^{2}=6.\]
Adding \(1\) to the first \(2n\) and subtracting \(1\) from the last \(n\) leaves each group's variance unchanged; new means are \(7\) and \(2\), new overall mean \(=\dfrac{2n\cdot7+n\cdot2}{3n}=\dfrac{16}{3}\).
\[k=\frac{2n\left(\sigma_1^{2}+(7-\tfrac{16}{3})^{2}\right)+n\left(\sigma_2^{2}+(2-\tfrac{16}{3})^{2}\right)}{3n}=\frac{2\sigma_1^{2}+\sigma_2^{2}+2\cdot\tfrac{25}{9}+\tfrac{100}{9}}{3}.\]
With \(2\sigma_1^{2}+\sigma_2^{2}=6\): \(k=\dfrac{6+\tfrac{150}{9}}{3}=\dfrac{68}{9}\), so \(9k=68.\)

For \(P=(x,y,z)\) the sum of squared distances from the three planes is
\[\frac{(x+y+z)^{2}}{3}+\frac{(lx-nz)^{2}}{l^{2}+n^{2}}+\frac{(x-2y+z)^{2}}{6}.\]
The locus \(x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}=9\) means this expression equals \(x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}\) identically.
Adding the first and third terms gives \(\tfrac12 x^{2}+y^{2}+\tfrac12 z^{2}+zx\). To reach \(x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}\), the middle term must supply \(\tfrac12 x^{2}+\tfrac12 z^{2}-zx\):
\[\frac{l^{2}}{l^{2}+n^{2}}=\frac12\Rightarrow l^{2}=n^{2},\qquad \frac{-2ln}{l^{2}+n^{2}}=-1\Rightarrow ln=l^{2}.\]
Hence \(n=l\), so \(l-n=0.\)
